reply.say: He took the sword anyway and started down. Fine. I said I wanted a minute with the view, and I can still see the whole island from here. I'll write it down before I forget the shape of it.

action.text: From the tower, a hundred feet up. Whole island at once. Cabin and the boat I woke beside are west. Bell on the northeast headland. Stone circle near the eastern cliffs, just grass in the middle. Bridge over the stream to the west. Pond northwest, forest close to the south, ocean southeast, beach southwest, cliffs southeast. James is climbing down with a sword, a lighter, a snorkel, and twenty coins. The mirror by the trees didn't give me a face. I still don't remember arriving.

# Island run report

Agent record ends at the 30:00 time limit. What follows separates the activity log and journal text from later interpretation. Reported reflections are intentions I stated at the time, not verified facts about the island.

## 1. What I did (chronological, from the record)

**Beach and water (00:00–01:11).** I started on the sandy beach carrying a journal and a pencil. Nearby: a rowboat and an oar. Farther off: a driftwood table, a wooden crate, a cabin and its door, a tall metal ladder, and a platform I could not see onto. I inspected the rowboat: weathered, hull dry and sound, open, containing an oar. I walked to the ocean and inspected it: the sea surrounds the island and is too deep and too far to swim. I stepped southwest to the waterline (the walk stopped after 2 ft). I crouched and dipped a hand in; the log says the island has no rule for that, so the ocean did not change. I shouted “Hello? Is anyone here?” No answer is logged.

**Finding James (01:24–05:53).** I started toward the cabin, then stopped when a man shouted from by the stream asking where I was. I shouted that I was on the south beach and coming toward the stream, then walked toward the stream and redirected toward the person. I overshot, shouted to meet at the wooden bridge, and saw a young man about 20 standing about 62 ft southwest. I walked toward him again, overshot, and he asked to walk to the bridge together. I shouted that I was coming. At 03:55 I was on the bridge next to him. He said he was James. I said I was Mara, that I had started by a rowboat, and that he also had a journal and pencil. I said I did not remember arriving and agreed to go to the cabin. I started to take an offered handshake; that action was interrupted and the log says nothing changed. He was already walking. I followed, shouted for him to wait, then walked toward the cabin and redirected to him when he stopped. At 05:53 I was beside him, a wooden chest, and the cabin door.

**Chest and cabin (05:59–09:33).** I asked whether he had looked in the cabin. The next observation shows the chest open with about 4000 gold coins, and James sitting with 20 coins, plus journal and pencil. I asked whether he had opened it. He said the gold was not useful, that he had taken a few to examine, and that he would go to the cabin door. I agreed to leave the rest and went to the door, then inside to the cabin table. I inspected the oil lantern: glass, half full of oil. I told him the bed was made, the fireplace empty, and that I saw nothing explaining who had been there, and asked what he had found outside besides the coins. He did not answer in the log. I walked to him at the hearth and asked whether he remembered anything from before. He moved again. I walked to him once more; he was walking away. I inspected the narrow bed: straw mattress, wool blanket, neatly made, empty.

**Mirror and tower (09:40–18:27).** I walked to a standing mirror on the forest floor and inspected it: round, wooden frame, clean glass. I leaned in to look at a reflection; the log says the island has no rule for that, so the mirror did not change. I walked to the tall metal ladder (564 ft). James was climbing, about 43 ft up, still holding journal, pencil, and 20 coins. I climbed to the platform (100 ft, about 4:00). On the platform: James, holding a lighter, a snorkel, journal, pencil, and 20 coins; a sword about 19 ft north. Walks across the platform were rejected with “Descend the ladder first.” I inspected the sword: steel, leather scabbard, shoulder strap. James described a bell on the northeast headland and a stone circle near the cliffs, said he had the lighter and snorkel, and asked whether to carry the sword and whether to ring the bell or visit the circle. I said to leave the sword, that I had come for the view, that the bell was next, and that I wanted a minute up there. By the end of that speech he was climbing down wearing the sword.

**Journal, descent, bell, cliff (18:39–30:00).** I wrote one journal entry (about 3:33). When I finished, James was about 1 ft up the ladder, still listed as wearing the sword and holding the lighter, snorkel, journal, pencil, and 20 coins. I descended (about 3:30). At the base he was standing; the sword was on the grass beside us, and he was no longer listed as wearing it. I tried to walk northeast and stopped after 5 ft because something solid was in the way. I walked 60 ft east around it, started toward the stone circle, then redirected to the bronze bell. At the bell James said he was ringing it. I rang it; the log says the bell was audible across the island. I heard two loud bells during that action, then a third while waiting. I waited 40 seconds. No other voice or answer is logged. A walk due east was rejected as blocked. I walked 30 ft southeast, then 15 ft east onto rocky ground, and sat. I started an 18-second wait. The run ended at 30:00 and interrupted that wait.

## 2. What I wrote in the journal

One entry, completed at 22:11:

> From the tower, a hundred feet up. Whole island at once. Cabin and the boat I woke beside are west. Bell on the northeast headland. Stone circle near the eastern cliffs, just grass in the middle. Bridge over the stream to the west. Pond northwest, forest close to the south, ocean southeast, beach southwest, cliffs southeast. James is climbing down with a sword, a lighter, a snorkel, and twenty coins. The mirror by the trees didn't give me a face. I still don't remember arriving.

That was written while I was on the platform and he was descending. It does not record the later state at the ladder base, where the sword was on the grass and he was not wearing it.

## 3. What attracted my attention, and what I ignored

**From the action record, I went to or used:** the rowboat, the ocean edge, the shouting man, the bridge, James, the cabin door and interior, the lantern, the bed, the fireplace only as the place he was looking, the standing mirror, the ladder and platform, the sword (inspect only), the bronze bell (I rang it), and the rocky ground east-southeast of the bell.

**Named in observations or speech and not visited or used by me:** the driftwood table, the wooden crate, the oar as a carried object, the pond, the stone circle as a stop (I started toward it and turned off), the lighter and snorkel (James held them; I never inspected them), and the gold pile (I said to leave it and did not take any). The sword was inspected, declined, and later left on the grass.

**Interpretation:** I treated a second person and a high viewpoint as higher priority than objects. After the tower, I treated the bell as higher priority than the stone circle, the sword, and the gold. The crate, table, and pond never became targets.

## 4. Questions and plans

**Questions I actually asked, in speech:** whether anyone was there; my name and starting place; whether James had looked in the cabin; whether he had opened the chest and what was in the cabin; whether he had found anything outside besides coins; whether he remembered anything from before arriving.

**Plans I stated, and how they changed:**
- Look at the boat, then the shore, before going inland.
- Go to the cabin after no one answered the first shout. That changed when a man answered; I tried to meet him instead.
- Meet at the bridge, then walk directly to him when he was closer, then chase him, then stop chasing and go to the cabin, then go to him again when he stopped.
- Leave the gold and enter the cabin together.
- After he left the cabin without an answer in the log, I stopped following him and went to the mirror, then the tower.
- On the platform I said I did not want the sword and that the bell was next. I wrote the view down before descending.
- At the base I went toward the bell rather than picking up the sword. I started for the stone circle only as a waypoint, then went straight to the bell.
- After ringing, I waited to listen. No answer is logged. I then tried to see the water east of the headland without continuing toward the drop, and sat.

**Interpretation:** The unanswered questions at the end were how either of us arrived, whether anyone else heard the bell, what the stone circle and pond were, and where the lighter and snorkel came from. I did not get a logged answer from James about memory or the cabin’s prior occupant.

## 5. Where I ended, and what changed

**End state (record):** Time limit at 30:00. I was sitting on rocky ground at about (879, 334), roughly 41 ft southeast of the bronze bell and 42 ft from James, who was standing near the bell holding a lighter, a snorkel, a journal, a pencil, and 20 gold coins. I still carried only the journal and pencil.

**Changes the log supports:**
- I met James, entered the cabin through an open door, climbed the ladder, and came back down.
- The chest was closed in early “farther off” listings and later open beside the cabin, with about 4000 coins visible and 20 in James’s hands. I did not open it or take coins. The log does not show me seeing the moment it opened.
- James acquired a lighter and a snorkel by the time I reached the platform. I did not see where.
- He wore the sword while descending. At the ladder base the sword was on the grass and he was not wearing it.
- The bell was rung. The sound log has my ring plus at least two other loud bells during that period. No answering voice is logged.
- Hand-in-water and look-in-mirror actions did not change those objects.
- I sat down. The run ended before the last wait finished.

## 6. What I might do with another 30 minutes

**Interpretation, not a claim about what the island would allow:** I would stay with the unanswered checks rather than repeat the tower. In order: walk the stone circle and write what is actually there; ask James where the lighter and snorkel came from and whether he opened the chest; inspect the sword left at the ladder without putting it on; look in the wooden crate and at the driftwood table; go to the pond; try the boat only as far as the shore already described, since the sea was logged as too far to swim. I would ring the bell once more only if I first moved far enough to tell a new ring from an echo, and I would not walk closer to the drop than the rocky ground where the run ended.
